text:
laura: FYI I pushed a small prototype of the "Scope Wizard" modal to PR #412 — it's in Figma and there's a working storybook slot. Need quick UX + policy input before we wire the API. Screenshot: https://figma.redwood/scope-wizard

imran: looked at the figma. big question: do we treat model scopes and route scopes as separate buckets (e.g., `models.read`, `models.generate`) or a single permission with qualifiers? enterprise customers asked for both patterns.

sara: prefer separate buckets in the UI but present them as grouped rules under a role. avoids one giant checklist. also we should show an "effective permissions" preview so admins see combined results.

josh: implementation note: backend will expose an eval endpoint to compute effective permissions. API sketch: `POST /v1/entitlements/eval { "role": { ... }, "resource": "route:generate" }` — can return allow/deny + reason. we'll need that for the preview.

marta: compliance asks for an optional "justification" field when a role grants write-level perms. also require audit-note if a role edits an entitlement affecting production routes.

laura: good call. UX idea: show a small red badge next to any permission that requires justification and collapse it by default. admins can expand to enter reason.

imran: question about scoping granularity: do we allow wildcard scopes like `models.*` and `routes.serviceX.*`? customers will want shorthand but that increases blast radius. we should prefer template roles (Billing Reader, Ops Deployer) + custom advanced mode.

sara: +1 for template-first. In the modal, top row -> role templates, middle -> granular toggles, bottom -> advanced JSON editor for custom policies. always show "preview as" button.

josh: dev note: the advanced JSON editor will accept a small DSL similar to existing policy format. example we can show in UI: ```json
{
  "principals": ["team:infra"],
  "actions": ["routes.invoke"],
  "resources": ["route:service-payment/*"],
  "effect": "allow"
}
```

marta: security: any custom policy must be validated server-side. deny-by-default and no implicit admin. also require an "owner" field for custom roles.

laura: UX question — do we surface token-scoped permissions in the same modal or a separate "API tokens" screen? some users expect role-to-token mapping inline.

imran: separate screen is simpler. mapping UI is a follow-up: "assign role to token" flow in Tokens page. don't overload the wizard.

sara: agree separate. we can include a small link in the wizard: "Assign to team/email/token" that opens mapping modal.

josh: backend needs: `role.create`, `role.update`, `role.preview` endpoints; plus audit log event for role changes. and a feature flag `rbac_scope_wizard_v1` for staged rollout.

ops-bot: audit: New RBAC preview invoked by laura at 2026-03-18T14:03:12Z (flag: rbac_scope_wizard_v1)

marta: also add an enterprise-only toggle for "delegate role management" so large customers can let sub-admins create roles limited to their org scope. this requires org-scoped role IDs.

laura: UX: if we add org-scoped roles we should show a banner: "You're creating an org-scoped role — only members of Org X can assign this role." small copy, :information_source:.

imran: rollout plan: behind feature flag, beta for dedicated customers, then opt-in via console for private deployments. logging/trace for each evaluation call to help debug preview mismatches.

sara: tiny polish: when someone toggles a permission that impacts production routes, show inline risk indicator and suggested mitigation (e.g., add canary route filter).

josh: can implement risk heuristics server-side (e.g., actions with `routes.*` + resource matching `prod-` get high risk). the preview can return risk level.

laura: ok action items I heard: 1) UX: add effective permissions preview + justification field + template-first layout; 2) Backend: add `entitlements/eval`, role CRUD, audit events, feature flag; 3) Security: server-side validation + org-scoped role support; 4) Docs: update RBAC guide + token mapping follow-up. I'll make a follow-up checklist in the PR.

imran: +1. can we also add a small CLI preview command for infra teams? `redwood rbac preview --role-file role.json --resource route:...` would be handy.

sara: love that. also add e2e tests for the preview modal to assert preview matches API.

marta: compliance: we want retention policy for role-change audit logs (default 7 years for enterprise). add to policy doc.

laura: thanks all — I'll update the figma and add the mockup for the justification input. tagging @imran @josh to help spec the eval endpoint. :thumbsup:

josh: I'll draft the API shape and feature flag branch tomorrow.

imran: i'll sketch the CLI subcommand after lunch.

laura: wrap-up: landing target for beta next week, gate: design sign-off + basic eval endpoint.

sara: :sparkles:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Feature flag `rbac_scope_wizard_v1` scheduled for canary rollout to internal orgs on 2026-03-22 03:00:00Z

laura: thanks everyone — I'll post updates in the PR and ping for quick reviews.
